chain.label: Captain and first officer fatigued from circadian disruption and extended wakefulness
chain.trigger: the captain had been awake for more than 19 hours, and the first officer had been awake for more than 12 hours

chain.label: Air Canada's non-salient presentation of NOTAM/ATIS runway 28L closure information
chain.trigger: the presentation of that information did not effectively convey the importance of the runway closure information and promote flight crew review and retention

chain.label: Flight crew failed to review/retain the runway 28L closure NOTAM in the flight release and ATIS
chain.trigger: neither crewmember recalled reviewing the specific NOTAM that described the runway closure

caused_by.evidence: the presentation of that information did not effectively convey the importance of the runway closure information and promote flight crew review and retention

chain.label: FMS Bridge approach chart's manual ILS-tuning instruction was not conspicuous; only approach requiring manual tuning
chain.trigger: the instruction on the approach chart to manually tune the ILS frequency was not conspicuous during the crew's review of the chart

chain.label: First officer omitted manually tuning the ILS frequency; captain failed to verify it during the approach briefing
chain.trigger: he did not enter the ILS frequency into the radio/navigation page... the captain did not verify, during the approach briefing, that the ILS frequency had been entered

caused_by.evidence: the FMS Bridge visual approach was the only approach in Air Canada's Airbus A320 database that required manual tuning for a navigational aid

chain.label: Flight crew, expecting SFO's usual open dual-runway configuration, misidentified taxiway C's airplane lights as runway 28R
chain.trigger: the flight crew's misidentification of taxiway C as the intended landing runway

caused_by.evidence: which resulted from the crewmembers' lack of awareness of the parallel runway closure due to their ineffective review of NOTAM information before the flight and during the approach briefing

the captain and the first officer were fatigued during the incident flight...which likely contributed to the crewmembers' misidentification of the intended landing surface, their ongoing expectation bias

chain.label: First officer's prolonged heads-down time completing missed-approach and runway-heading tasks after F101D reduced approach monitoring
chain.trigger: the first officer's focus on tasks inside the cockpit after the airplane passed the final waypoint reduced his opportunity to effectively monitor the approach

caused_by.evidence: the captain and the first officer were fatigued during the incident flight

chain.label: Captain made the turn at F101D and aligned the airplane with taxiway C instead of runway 28R
chain.trigger: the captain made the required 14° right turn to align the airplane with runway 28R but instead aligned the airplane with taxiway C

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew's misidentification of taxiway C as the intended landing runway
the crewmembers could not take advantage of the ILS's lateral guidance capability to help ensure proper surface alignment
neither crewmember realized, once the airplane passed the final waypoint, that the airplane was not aligned with the intended landing runway

chain.label: Despite perceiving lights across the surface and querying ATC, crew continued the approach after the tower confirmed the runway was clear
chain.trigger: the flight crewmembers were unable to reconcile their confusion about the perceived lights on the runway...with the controller's assurance that the runway was clear

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was lined up with taxiway C
once the airplane was aligned with what the flight crewmembers thought was the correct landing surface, they were likely not strongly considering contradictory information

chain.label: Crew recognized misalignment cues near the seawall and initiated a low-altitude go-around, overflying four airplanes on taxiway C (as low as 60 ft) and averting collision with no injury or damage
chain.trigger: the incident flight crew initiated a go-around...None of the 5 flight crewmembers and 135 passengers aboard the incident airplane were injured, and the incident airplane was not damaged

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew initiated a low-altitude go-around
the airplane descended to an altitude of 100 ft above ground level and overflew the first airplane on the taxiway
